findings.title: Org scope ignores direct org memberships when there are no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only fetches user memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, even though teamIds always includes options.orgId. For an organization with no child teams, direct org memberships are skipped, so the condition only allows team bookings and excludes personal bookings of org members. When at least one child team exists, those same org memberships are included, making the authorization behavior inconsistent and potentially returning incomplete insights.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation depends on unordered repository result order
findings.body: The test expects Prisma.sql values containing teamIds and userIds in a fixed order, but the service builds those arrays from repository queries without explicit ordering. Since ANY array order is semantically irrelevant but toEqual compares array order, the test can be flaky if the database returns teams or memberships in a different order. Sorting the IDs before building the SQL or comparing unordered sets would be safer.

findings.title: Database test does not exercise array ANY raw SQL conditions
findings.body: The only $queryRaw execution uses the user-scope condition, which has no array parameters. The org and team authorization paths that use teamId = ANY(...) and userId = ANY(...) are only compared as Prisma.sql objects. If Prisma or the Postgres driver does not bind these array parameters as intended, the integration tests will not catch the failure despite this being a raw-SQL conversion.
